claims.finding: The stock has fully round-tripped the 31 July NXP takeover pop (67.01 on 29 Jun -> 86.00 on 31 Jul -> 63.38 at the print), so it enters the print at a level BELOW its pre-rumour price and roughly 18% below the reported ~$3.3bn deal value, while no denial or withdrawal from Ambarella or NXP appears anywhere in the capture - the approach is unresolved, undenied, and now valued at zero by the tape.

claims.why_not_priced: The rumour itself is wire copy (FT/Reuters, 31 July) and is priced - twice, up then down. What is not priced is the asymmetry it creates at this specific price: an undenied approach at ~$77/share sitting under a $63 stock means a bad print cannot re-rate the equity down toward its standalone trough as freely as the 16.8% median reaction implies, because the strategic bid is a live alternative bid for the asset. If the market were treating the approach as dead AND the fundamentals as fine, the stock would not be 26% off its 7 August high on falling volume; if it were treating the approach as live, it would not be trading below the pre-rumour price.
claims.independence: filings.json shows the insider-selling cadence stopped abruptly: 144s and Form 4s were filed roughly monthly through 2026-07-09/07-10 and then nothing at all for the eight weeks into the print, longer than a routine quarterly blackout, which is weakly consistent with a live M&A process rather than a dead one - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1280263/000128026326000055/xslF345X06/edgardoc.xml
